doc.title: Michael Max Fleming interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017

chapter: Rahsaan Roland Kirk and the jazz peak
title: Recording with Rahsaan Roland Kirk
summary: He made two records with Kirk, Gifts and Messages and I Talk with the Spirits. They played the gig material in the studio, with no charts, counts or keys.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Can you describe for me what let’s say the late 60s, if you were doing a record date with Rahsaan or anybody else, what exactly, how much time you got in the studio and what was the pressure like. Was there pressure?

Okay. Okay I did two records with Rahsaan. The one “I Talk with the Spirits,” you may have run across that where it’s “Serenade to a Cuckoo” — that’s me. Okay? For me — and that was my second record. My first record I made with him they didn’t put my name on the record jacket. So that was traumatic.
What was the name of the record?

That was on Mercury, right after Mercury turned into Limelight. So, and on the track he announces my name so that’s better than — because a jacket can get torn, so it’s almost indelible. Not really indelible but it’s right on the record as opposed to being on the liner notes. But what are you asking, what was it like?
Were you more critical of your own playing because you knew you were going to hear it back? Did you play differently?

With him it was one thing, with him the records I made basically we played what we played on the gig. We didn’t write charts. I made up my parts. Nobody gave me a part. The whole group we just — it was a beautiful thing in a way. And so when we went into the studio I was nervous on that first record. But we were playing what we played every night. Everything he did was so spontaneous. You never knew what he was going to do. He never counted off the tunes. He never gave keys. He just started playing.
I just got this image of you and the piano player like, you know, one of you whispering to the other what key we’re in or something?
